title: NHC blended Google DeepMind's AI ensemble into official Hurricane Melissa forecasts before its Category 5 landfall in Jamaica
summary: NHC blended Google DeepMind's AI ensemble into official Melissa forecasts from its first advisory on 21 Oct 2025; Cat 5 landfall in Jamaica 28 Oct 2025.
account: From its first advisory on 21 October 2025, the US National Hurricane Center (NHC) blended Google DeepMind's experimental AI hurricane model (ensemble mean GDMI) into its official forecasts for Tropical Storm Melissa: Discussion 1 placed the official track between the DeepMind ensemble mean and the consensus aid HCCA, and Discussion 2 described the track as a blend of the DeepMind mean, HCCA and TVCA. Discussion 8 (23 October) moved the track toward a blend of the DeepMind mean and HCCA; Discussion 10 blended the HCCA and GDMI aids and set an intensity forecast in best agreement with GDMI after all 50 DeepMind members showed a major hurricane. On 28 October 2025 Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope with 185 mph winds and 892 mb pressure. IFRC reported 45 deaths and about 1.6 million people affected, and relayed a World Bank/IDB estimate of US$8.8 billion in physical damage; its CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF was approved on 23 October with a five-day lead time.
purpose: Experimental AI tropical cyclone forecast model providing ensemble track and intensity guidance to NHC forecasters.
system: Google DeepMind AI hurricane forecast model, ensemble mean designated GDMI in NHC guidance
taxonomy_note: Loose fit: hazard forecast accuracy for public safety; the taxonomy has no early-warning category.

ratings.reason: No fetched source attributes an individual-level outcome to the AI guidance; impacts are reported only at population level.
NHC's official track and intensity forecasts were materially shaped by GDMI (Discussions 8, 10, 13, 14), and NHC's Science Operations Officer called the AI guidance very valuable for Melissa.

Official forecasts for a Category 5 landfall affecting about 1.6 million people, and a CHF 80,000 Imminent DREF approved on 23 October with a five-day lead time whose early actions the review says were informed by forecast risks (NHC is not named); material to many, but no counterfactual that the AI changed outcomes.

ai_role.statement: NHC forecasters state in Discussions 8, 10, 12, 13 and 14 that official track and intensity forecasts were blended with or aligned to the Google DeepMind ensemble; the official forecast remains a human synthesis of several aids, so the AI contribution to outcomes in Jamaica is not isolated.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.
Paired with AI Incident Database incident 1546 (medium confidence); severity not given by the source.

Set the date observed to 21 October 2025 and reworded the summary and account because Discussions 1 and 2 show the Google DeepMind ensemble mean shaping the official track from the first advisory, added those two discussions as evidence, corrected the Discussion 14 title to 'Tropical Storm Melissa' as its header reads, attributed the US$8.8 billion damage figure to the World Bank/IDB estimate relayed by IFRC, and tied the DREF's early actions to 'forecast risks' as the review says rather than to NHC.
